The Exaltation of the Holy Cross

Icons

Feasts

The Exaltation of the Holy Cross

Elevation of the Cross · Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

1 Corinthians 1:18–24

John 19:17–35

John 12:28–36

King James Version · Scripture previews

Holy Cross parish’s published feast account commemorates the finding of Christ’s Cross and its elevation before the people. It gives September 14 as the church-calendar feast date; this label does not itself select a civil-calendar equivalent.

[1] Introduction; Background

What is depicted

The icon type shows Patriarch Macarius lifting the Cross from the pulpit. Clergy and laypeople gather around him, including Saint Helen; deacons carry candles. The article explains the composition through the Church’s traditional narrative of the Cross’s discovery in Jerusalem.

[1] Icon of the Feast

History and tradition

In the published tradition, Helen finds three crosses, a healing identifies Christ’s Cross, and Macarius raises it so the people can see. This is the feast account’s sacred narrative, distinct from the date and provenance of any surviving icon.

[1] Background, paragraphs 1–4

The selected Palekh icon is dated to the middle of the nineteenth century in its file record.

[2] File description and displayed historic reproduction

Published explanation

The parish reads the feast as the transformation of an instrument of shame into a sign of victory over death. It connects the Cross with the universality of redemption and the contrast between divine and worldly wisdom.

[1] Background, final two paragraphs

For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God.

[3] 1 Corinthians 1:18
